{{Short description|British mathematician and Kenyan missionary}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Edward Carey Francis''' [[OBE]], (13 September 1897 – 27 July 1966)<ref name=Pars1968>{{cite journal|last1=Pars|first1=L. A.|title=Edward Carey Francis|journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society|date=1968|volume=s1-43|issue=1|page=368|doi=10.1112/jlms/s1-43.1.368}}</ref> was a British [[mathematician]] and Anglican missionary to [[Kenya]], where he became "arguably the most influential educationist in Kenya's modern history".<ref name="BaleSang2013">{{cite book|author1=John Bale|author2=Joe Sang|title=Kenyan Running: Movement Culture, Geography and Global Change|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WUzdAAAAQBAJ&pg=PA81|year= 2013|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-135-24626-6|pages=81–}}</ref>

He was born in [[Hampstead]], [[London]]. He was educated first at [[William Ellis School]], becoming head-boy of the school and captain of the [[cricket]], [[association football|football]], [[tennis]] and [[Sport of athletics|athletics]] teams.<ref name=Pars1968/>  After school he enlisted in the [[British Army]], serving in the [[First World War]] with the [[Royal Field Artillery]]<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=30326|page=10376|date=5 October 1917|supp=y}}</ref> and being [[mentioned in despatches]].<ref name="auto">Robert M. Maxon, Thomas P. Ofcansky, Historical Dictionary of Kenya, Rowman & Littlefield, 9 Sep 2014, p.75</ref> On completion of the war he took up a scholarship to read mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref name="Pars1968"/>

After graduating, in 1922 he became a fellow of [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]] and Director of Studies in Mathematics. He left Cambridge in 1928 when he joined the [[Church Missionary Society]].<ref name="Pars1968"/>  He was posted to Kenya and became firstly a teacher and later Headmaster of [[Maseno School]] in [[Nyanza Province|Nyanza]] between 1928 and 1940. He shortly served as Mathematics teacher at Duke of York School ([[Lenana School]]). He then served as Headmaster at [[Alliance High School (Kenya)|Alliance High School]] between 1940 and 1962. During his time at Alliance he developed a mythical-like reputation as an inspiring teacher, educating many future politicians.<ref name="Pars1968"/> In later years, between 1962 and 1966 he was Assistant Master at Pumwani High School.<ref name="auto"/> In Jomo Kenyatta's first cabinet, nine out of the fifteen members had studied under Francis at Alliance.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kiereini |first1=Douglas |title=Carey Francis: Discipline, academic excellence were non-negotiable|url=https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/lifestyle/society/Carey-Francis/3405664-4864278-ynrcarz/index.html |website=[[Business Daily Africa|Business Daily]] |date=November 22, 2018}}</ref>

Francis died in Nairobi on 27 July 1966 and was buried within the grounds of Alliance High School.<ref name="Pars1968"/> On his death, a silence was held in the [[House of Representatives (Kenya)|House of Representatives]], an honour usually reserved for Heads of State.<ref name="Pars1968"/>
